rationale: CP1 (#736 cpp wave): the analyzer emitted NO bare-identifier edges at all (`return g;` produced zero relationships) while the oracle audited only calls/member reads — a both-sides blind spot. Every bare identifier naming a file-visible VALUE is now a Uses edge with C-family discipline: locals/params shadow (h shadows g_var), member reads resolve in member functions (bump reads count), namespace members resolve inside their namespace or via using-directives (x), callbacks read as values (target_fn), enumerators read in case labels (RED), explicit-template callees stay calls-only (ident, no uses). Static free functions are private (HC1/CP3 parity). M60/#924: the CP7 pin below names the method `step`, not `Inner::step` — the qualified spelling was the outer-segment name read, not a contract.

expectRelationships.comment: CP5: out-of-line member read resolves through Foo

CP7: nested out-of-line resolves through the innermost class. #924 changed the SOURCE spelling only: the old name `Inner::step` was the outer qid's last segment read as a name (the same read that published `string to_string` from a misplaced return type), so it carried the owner inline. The method's name is `step` and its owner is `Inner` — which is exactly the innermost-class resolution this pin has always been about, and the target (`n`) is unchanged.
CP6: bindings suppress only the bound names; other globals still read
